stories.headline: How India Avoided An LPG Shortage Amid West Asia War | Hardeep Singh Puri
stories.title: How India Avoided An LPG Shortage Amid West Asia War | Hardeep Singh Puri
stories.summary: Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri has explained how India managed its energy supplies amid global geopolitical tensions and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. Puri said India had approximately 60 days of crude oil and natural gas supplies even under an extreme disruption scenario. However, LPG remained a concern because three major suppliers – Qatar, the UAE and Saudi Arabia – are located near the Strait of Hormuz. To strengthen domestic availability, India ramped up daily LPG production from around 35,000 metric tonnes to 55,000 metric tonnes. Puri credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and cooperation between public and private sector companies, claiming that not one of India's 1.07 lakh retail outlets ran dry.

article_sentences: This moisture-laden air is expected to contribute to cloud formation and rainfall across parts of the state.
Patna: The impact of cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’, which has developed over the Bay of Bengal, is beginning to be felt in Bihar, with clouds covering several areas, including Patna, early on Friday.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast unsettled weather and light rainfall in several districts, along with a warning of lightning strikes.
According to the Meteorological Department, 13 districts may experience a change in weather conditions on Friday.
These include Patna, Nalanda, Jehanabad, Arwal, Gaya, Sheikhpura, Lakhisarai, Aurangabad, Jamui, Nawada, Banka, Bhagalpur and Munger.
Light rain is possible in these areas, while residents have been advised to remain cautious due to the possibility of lightning.
The weather is expected to remain unsettled in several parts of Bihar on November 21 and 22 as well, as the cyclonic system gradually influences weather conditions across eastern India.
The department has forecast light rainfall in Supaul, Araria, Kishanganj, Saharsa, Madhepura, Purnea, Katihar, Khagaria, Munger, Bhagalpur, Banka and Jamui during this period.
A warning of heavy rainfall has specifically been issued for Bhagalpur and Katihar.
Meteorologists said the system is likely to influence wind patterns over Bihar, bringing easterly winds carrying moisture from the Bay of Bengal.
According to the forecast, cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ is expected to move towards the vicinity of the Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts by Friday.
Wind speeds over the sea could reach 90-100 kmph, indicating the intensity of the weather system.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Light rain in parts of Jharkhand; primary classes suspended in some districts

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Parts of Jharkhand experienced light rainfall on Friday (November 20, 2026) morning under the influence of Cyclone Akvan as some district authorities suspended primary classes in schools, an official said.
The landfall process of the cyclone commenced near Gopalpur in Odisha around 8 a.m.

Rainfall is expected to intensify in the afternoon, as the IMD has issued an 'orange' alert (be prepared) for heavy downpour in five Jharkhand districts till 8.30 a.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026), the official said.
East Singhbhum and Saraikela-Kharswan district administrations have ordered schools to suspend primary classes on Friday (November 20, 2026) in view of the cyclone.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an 'orange' alert for heavy rainfall in Dhanbad, Bokaro, Seraikela-Kharswan, and East and West Singhbhum districts till 8.30 a.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
A 'yellow' alert (be updated) for heavy rain has been issued for Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Ranchi, Khunti, Ramgarh and Jamtara for the same period, a weather bulletin said.
"The rainfall is likely to intensify later in the day and some districts may experience very heavy rainfall.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely in some places along with gusty winds of up to 50 kmph speed," Ranchi Meteorological Centre Deputy Director Abhishek Anand said.
He said the situation is expected to improve from November 22 and clear skies are likely from November 23.

article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan brings heavy rainfall to southern West Bengal, disrupting transport in Kolkata as the IMD issues warnings for coastal districts and advises fishermen to stay away from the sea until Saturday.
Kolkata: Cyclone Akvan triggered rain across several southern districts of West Bengal, with the IMD forecasting downpours in the region till Saturday.

The cyclonic storm, which made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha, brought incessant light to moderate rain in Kolkata, leading to disruptions in public transport and causing inconvenience to office-goers during the morning peak hours on Friday.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast very heavy rain over the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur till Saturday.
Several other districts of south Bengal will receive heavy rain till Saturday owing to the effect of the cyclone.
The Met office forecast light to moderate rain in Kolkata, with one or two spells of heavy rain on Friday.
The city received 19.2 mm of rainfall in 24 hours till 8.30 am on Friday, while Medinipur recorded the state's highest precipitation during the period at 47 mm, according to the IMD data.
The IMD advised fishermen not to venture into the sea along and off the West Bengal coast till Saturday, as sea conditions remain rough.

stories.headline: Rajasthan panchayat election results: Congress takes early lead; 5 reasons why these polls matter
stories.title: Rajasthan panchayat election results: Congress takes early lead; 5 reasons why these polls matter
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'election results' in title weight 64
article_sentences: Almost three years into Bhajan Lal Sharma taking the oath as Rajasthan Chief Minister, the second major test of his government is underway Friday in the counting of votes for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti candidates in 37 out of 41 districts.
In December 2023, the BJP had virtually sidelined all its major faces in Rajasthan, including two-term former CM Vasundhara Raje, and experimented with Sharma — a first-time MLA.
Along the way, there have been a few hiccups and setbacks, with Sharma benefitting from his clean image but often ailing from alleged indecisiveness.
However, at the party level, it became crystal clear that the party, and not individual leaders in the state, are supreme.
The cult of personality associated with Raje and some second-rung leaders in the state was wiped out bit by bit, in 2023, and in the years before and after.

In these circumstances, the Panchayat Raj Institutions (PRI) polls are being seen as an indicator and a measure of the success – or limitations – of that experiment: from a more centralised process to a decentralised one.

The urban local body polls in September indicated partial success with the difference between the BJP and the Congress in terms of vote share being just 0.91 per cent even as the ruling party went on to form Boards in most of the urban bodies.

The Urban Local Bodies (ULB) polls also indicated that if the BJP lacked in electoral strength, it made up for it through organisational heft; however, the BJP’s wins also came amid alleged coercive action by authorities.
While the BJP is considered more of an urban party, the Congress sees its strength in rural areas.
However, in Rajasthan, the ruling party generally fares better in both urban and rural local body polls.
Having come very close to the BJP in terms of numbers in urban polls, the Congress is upbeat about the PRI results.
Over the past few weeks, its leaders have maintained that the party will fare better in the PRI polls than it did in urban polls.

stories.headline: Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs’ appointment case
stories.title: Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs’ appointment case
stories.summary: The CJI also said the five-judge Bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) declined a submission to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict delivered by a two-judge bench on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger bench.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the recall application, as well as any challenge to the reference order, could be considered by the five-judge Constitution Bench already constituted to hear the batch of petitions challenging the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
The CJI also said the five-judge Bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict.

Advocate Bhushan said that the recall application should be listed before the original bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which delivered the split verdict on September 23.
He pointed out that Justice Sharma was due to retire next week.
Advocate Bhushan further said that Justice Sharma had a conflict of interest and, therefore, the application seeking recall of the verdict ought to be heard by the same bench.
When the CJI suggested that the reference bench could consider the application, Advocate Bhushan said the reference order itself was recalled on the ground of an alleged conflict of interest.
However, the CJI said that the issue could be raised before the five-judge Constitution bench, which has been constituted for final adjudication of the constitutional challenge to the 2023 law.
The development follows a split verdict delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on whether the petitions challenging the 2023 law warranted consideration by a larger bench.
The main objection was the exclusion of the CJI from the panel to select the CEC and ECs.
The panel now includes the prime minister, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and a cabinet minister.

While Justice Datta was of the view that the challenge could be adjudicated by a two-judge bench, Justice Sharma favoured a reference to a five-judge Constitution bench, considering the significant constitutional questions involved.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs Probe Into Why Registry Refused To List ED Plea Against Bail For Over Three Years
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs Probe Into Why Registry Refused To List ED Plea Against Bail For Over Three Years
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday(November 20) directed its Secretary General to conduct a fact-finding enquiry and submit a report explaining why a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate in 2023 challenging a bail order was not listed for hearing for more than three years despite a judicial direction.

The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against the grant of bail to Raman Singla.
Notice in the matter had been issued in 2023, yet the case was never listed for over three years.
"Why has this matter not been listed?
September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, September 2026.
This is what I want to know," CJI Surya Kant asked at the outset.
Justice Bagchi described that situation as "institutional lethargy."

Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Singla, said that such a situation should not occur in the Supreme Court and that the Registry “can't be managed like that.” Dave remarked that he had “never seen this happen in the Supreme Court.”
"Maybe because you have not been in the Supreme Court Registry," retorted Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain, who was representing the ED.
"I have been here twice the number of years you have practised, Mr Hossain," responded Dave.
"As an Advocate-on-Record I mean," Hossain clarified.
"Since 1990, I have been practising.

stories.headline: Assam Cabinet Approves Six New Municipal Boards, Land Allotment for Defence and Agricultural Institute
stories.title: Assam Cabinet Approves Six New Municipal Boards, Land Allotment for Defence and Agricultural Institute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: GUWAHATI: The Assam Cabinet, which met in New Delhi today, took several decisions, including land allotment to the Ministry of Defence and expanding the areas of local urban bodies.
The cabinet has approved the allotment of 74 bighas of land in the Sonitpur district to the Ministry of Defence.
It also approved the allotment of 1,568 bighas of government land in Dhemaji for the setting up of an Indian Agriculture Research Institute.
To improve urban governance, the Cabinet has approved the creation of six new municipal boards, one each at Laluk, Harmutty-Bandardea, Ghilamara, Majuli, Udarbond, and Mirza-Bijay Nagar.
It also approved area expansion and ward delimitation in 23 existing urban local bodies.
The cabinet has approved classifying areas as urban areas only from 1 km from the town limits to facilitate larger land allocations for indigenous communities under Mission Basundhara 4.0.
This decision will not be applicable for the Kamrup (M) and Kamrup districts.
The cabinet has approved the enhancement of remuneration of the elected representatives of Panchayat Raj Institutes, Zila Parishad, Anchalik Parishads and Gaon Panchayats.
This will benefit presidents, vice-presidents and members of such bodies.

The cabinet has approved the amendment of the Matak Autonomous Council Act, the Kamatapur Autonomous Council Act, and the Moran Autonomous Council Act for conducting elections to the general councils of these autonomous councils on a non-political party basis.
